videoIdeas.title: Nobody Can Speak Anymore
videoIdeas.hook: The amount of people who can't string a sentence together in a room full of humans is genuinely embarrassing.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your own post on this exact theme (DbilFRjsJ3v) pulled 635 views with a weak caption and no clear payoff. It's an underused pillar for you, and 'people can't communicate anymore' is a format doing numbers for lifeofdinoo_ (phone addiction, red pill critiques). Sharpen it into a proper argument and it'll travel.
videoIdeas.script: The amount of people who can't string a sentence together in a room full of humans is genuinely embarrassing. And it's not their fault — nobody trained them. You spent ten years typing and zero years talking. So now you freeze the second someone puts you on the spot. Here's the fix, and it's not confidence. Confidence is a myth people sell you. It's reps. Start talking out loud when nobody's watching. Read a page from a book like you're explaining it to your little brother. Record it. Listen back. Yeah it's painful. That pain is the skill forming. Do that for two weeks and the next time you're asked to speak, your mouth won't betray you. You don't rise to the occasion. You fall to your level of practice.

visuals.setting: Static talking-head, sat down, plain wall or car, natural light, plain fitted top. Calm, low energy, direct eye contact — the older-brother-cornering-you-at-a-family-event vibe.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'you type all day and can't speak for 30 seconds' appears as you say the first line, hard cut into your face mid-sentence.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on you awkwardly stumbling through an intro then freeze-frame: 'this is most of you'
Silent 2-second stare at camera before the first word lands
On-screen caption counter ticking '10 years typing / 0 years talking'

videoIdeas.title: Competent AND Trustworthy — Pick Both
videoIdeas.hook: Everyone wants to be a leader. Almost nobody wants to be trustworthy first.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your prophetic leadership post (DTauCL6jJ8Z) got 508 views and 58 likes — a strong like-to-view ratio, meaning the people who saw it valued it. Leadership is a core pillar you barely post. Reframe the Al-Qawi wal-Ameen concept into a punchy standalone rather than a caption-heavy carousel.
videoIdeas.script: Everyone wants to be a leader. Almost nobody wants to be trustworthy first. In the Quran the standard is Al-Qawi wal-Ameen — strong and trustworthy. Notice the order people ignore. We obsess over the strength. The following, the influence, the platform. And we skip the trust entirely. Here's the problem. Competence without trust makes you dangerous. You've met that person. Sharp, capable, and you wouldn't leave your wallet in the room with them. That's not a leader. That's a liability with good PR. Real authority is when people would follow you even when no one's checking. Build that first. The influence you're chasing is downstream of the character you're skipping.

visuals.setting: Talking head, slightly more composed setting — desk, books behind, or masjid courtyard. Measured tone, this one is teaching not ranting.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text splits into two columns 'STRONG' and 'TRUSTWORTHY' with the second one flashing red/underlined as you say 'almost nobody.'
otherHookIdeas: Open on the Arabic 'Al-Qawi wal-Ameen' on screen, then translate it live
Pattern interrupt: 'you've met a smart person you wouldn't trust with £20' pulled to the front
Hold up a physical book/mushaf and point to the concept

videoIdeas.title: Third Spaces Aren't Cringe, They're Survival
videoIdeas.hook: People are mocking young Muslims for opening cafés and study circles. They've got it completely backwards.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your third spaces post (Dbwq4JosFxD) already hit 931 views — proof the topic lands. But the caption got cut off and the argument wasn't fully delivered on camera. This is a community-leadership angle that's genuinely yours, and 'building vs complaining' is exactly the older-brother framing your niche is missing.
videoIdeas.script: People are mocking young Muslims for opening cafés and study circles. They've got it completely backwards. For years the complaint was: we've got nowhere to go, no community, everything's a pub or a club. Now people are actually building the alternative — hubs, socials, study circles, places you can walk into and belong. And the response from the sidelines is 'this is cringe.' No. This is leadership. Building something imperfect beats criticising something that doesn't exist. Every institution you respect started as a few people in a small room who were probably mocked. You can be the person who builds the room, or the person who tweets about the room. One of those gets remembered.

visuals.setting: Film in an actual café or community space if possible — walking-and-talking or leaning against a table. Warm, real environment, not a bedroom. Casual but sharp.
visuals.visualHook: Cold open mid-action walking into a café/community space, camera following, first line delivered as you sit down.
otherHookIdeas: On-screen text 'building > tweeting about building' as a punchline mid-video
B-roll of an empty room filling with people as you talk about belonging
Direct-to-camera: 'you can build the room or tweet about it' pulled forward as the hook

videoIdeas.title: Your Aunty Has Opinions, Not Information
videoIdeas.hook: Every uncle and aunty has an opinion on your degree. Not one of them has read a green paper.
videoIdeas.rationale: This is nearly verbatim your caption from Dc83y8Zs8Fh (779 views) — but that post never fully cashed in the idea on camera. It's a perfect blend of your bite and a relatable young-Muslim tension. birdtart01 crushes with strict/immigrant-parent themes; this is your articulate version of that lane.
videoIdeas.script: Every uncle and aunty has an opinion on your degree. Not one of them has read a green paper. And that's the trap you keep falling into — mistaking loud for informed. There's a difference between someone who can fix the thing and someone who decides whether the thing gets built at all. We've got plenty of the first. Engineers, doctors, coders. We've got almost none of the second. Policy, decision-making, the rooms where things actually get chosen. Everyone told you to be useful. Nobody told you to be in the room. So here's the shift. Stop asking 'what job pays.' Start asking 'who decides.' That's where your community's been absent for two generations, and it's costing you more than any salary.

visuals.setting: Talking head, slightly wry energy, this one has a smirk in it. Living room or car. Conversational, like you're saying what everyone's thinking at the dinner table.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'opinions ≠ information' stamped over a freeze of your face raising an eyebrow.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open impersonating the aunty line ('so what are you going to do with THAT degree') then cut to you: 'she hasn't read a green paper'
On-screen text punchline 'we can fix the thing, we can't decide whether it gets built'
Pattern interrupt with a quick zoom on 'who decides?'

videoIdeas.title: Stop Making Refutation Your Personality
videoIdeas.hook: Half of you spend more energy correcting other Muslims than you've ever spent on the people actually attacking us.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your posts DZTRC2KMKuU (1045 views, 108 likes) and DWCTOehDMTr both hit this 'stop the infighting, focus on what's dire' nerve and performed well with high engagement. This is a signature theme for you — package it as a clean standalone rather than reactive commentary tied to one incident, so it stays evergreen.
videoIdeas.script: Half of you spend more energy correcting other Muslims than you've ever spent on the people actually attacking us. Every day it's a new refutation. A new thread on who's off the manhaj. A new video pointing out someone's mistake. And meanwhile your brothers and sisters are being bombed, displaced, erased — and you've got nothing to say about that because it doesn't get you engagement. Be honest. The infighting feels good because it's easy. You get to feel righteous without doing anything hard. Correcting someone online costs you nothing. Actually building, actually helping, actually organising — that costs. So ask yourself which one you're addicted to. The ummah doesn't need more critics with wifi. It needs people who can tell the difference between what matters and what just feels good to say.

visuals.setting: Talking head, serious, lower energy, minimal background. This one is the older brother going quiet and honest — no smirk. Slight lean into the camera.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'critics with wifi' appears bold and holds as the first line is delivered flat and direct.
otherHookIdeas: Silent stare then the line — let the discomfort sit
On-screen text tally: 'refutations posted: 47 / people helped: 0'
Hard cut from a scrolling comments section to your face

videoIdeas.title: Nervous Isn't A Reason, It's An Excuse
videoIdeas.hook: 'I get too nervous to speak' — nobody's asking you to be fearless. They're asking you to do it scared.
videoIdeas.rationale: Public speaking is your weakest-covered pillar despite being one of three core ones. The 'do it scared' mindset angle bridges public speaking and mindset, and short punchy reframes are exactly the format doing well for lifeofdinoo_ and birdtart01. Gives you a repeatable series 'speaking fixes.'
videoIdeas.script: 'I get too nervous to speak.' Nobody's asking you to be fearless. They're asking you to do it scared. You've built this fantasy where one day the nerves vanish and then you'll finally speak up. That day isn't coming. The people you admire, the ones who command a room — they're nervous too. The difference is they stopped waiting to feel ready. Nerves aren't a stop sign. They're a tax. You pay it and you go anyway. And here's the part nobody tells you: the nerves shrink on the other side of doing it, never before. So the next time your heart's pounding and you want to stay quiet — that's exactly the moment your name should be the first one heard. Waiting to feel ready is just fear wearing a polite outfit.

visuals.setting: Talking head, punchy medium energy. Plain background. Fast delivery, a bit of edge. Good candidate for a hard-cut edit style.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'do it scared' slams on screen with a quick zoom-in on your face at the em-dash.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open: 'the nerves never leave — sorry' as a pattern interrupt
On-screen text punchline 'fear wearing a polite outfit' timed to the last line
Quick cut montage of a hand raising / mic being taken before the talking head lands

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Your best post ever at 6138 views. The caption opens with a dated, timely provocation ('still discussing... in 2026') that creates immediate friction and urgency — this is your voice at its sharpest and the algorithm rewarded the debate it started (15 comments).
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The caption gets cut off mid-thought ('feel bett...') and the argument trails into a vague dig. Land the point cleanly in the first two lines so the payoff isn't hidden behind a 'more' tap. Timely political heat brought the reach — now convert those one-time viewers by tying the topic back to one of your three pillars so they know what they're following you for.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 2108 views with 136 likes — that's a strong like-to-view ratio, meaning people who watched strongly agreed. The specific, named callout ('UAE Hijrah bros', 'Faris Hammadi') gives it teeth and specificity, which is far more shareable than vague commentary.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 5 comments despite the likes — it's a mic-drop that people nodded at but didn't feel invited to argue with. End on an open question ('is this really hijrah or just a rebrand?') to convert agreement into comments, which is what pushes reach. Also the caption cuts off again — tighten it.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your public speaking pillar showing up directly and the premise ('people can't string a sentence together') is genuinely strong and relatable — it's the seed of one of your best possible content lanes.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 635 views, 29 likes, 0 comments — it underperformed because it diagnosed a problem without delivering a fix or a sharp payoff. People don't share a complaint; they share a solution or a line that stings. Rework it with an actual method (reps, recording yourself) and a closing line worth quoting. This topic deserves a proper standalone, not a passing observation.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 1045 views with 108 likes and 13 comments — excellent engagement across the board. The 'stop the infighting, focus on what's dire' theme clearly resonates hard with your audience and is emotionally charged in your voice. This is a signature topic for you.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: It reads as reactive to a specific person/moment, which caps its shelf life. Repackage this exact sentiment as an evergreen standalone (see the 'critics with wifi' idea) so it keeps getting served for months instead of dying with the news cycle. Also open with the accusation, not the wind-up.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 508 views but 58 likes — one of your highest like-to-view ratios, and the only clear leadership-pillar post in the set. The Al-Qawi wal-Ameen framing is substantive and differentiated; the people who saw it valued it highly.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The reach was low because it's caption-and-carousel heavy ('11 Prophetic Qualities...') rather than a punchy hook-driven video. This concept can carry a whole video on its own — lead on camera with 'everyone wants strength, nobody wants to be trustworthy' and let the Quranic frame be the reveal, not the setup. Leadership is a core pillar you barely post; feed it more.
